headline: Mexico welcomes home ancient Aztec codex after nearly two centuries
meta_description: The Codex Azcatitlán, held in France for 125 years, goes on display in Mexico City for the first time in 186 years, marking a milestone in cultural repatriatio…
summary_short: A priceless 16th-century Aztec manuscript depicting the fall of the Aztec civilization returns to Mexico after 186 years away, on loan from France.
body:
After nearly two centuries abroad, one of the most significant chronicles of Aztec history is coming home. The Codex Azcatitlán, a 16th-century pictographic manuscript documenting the Aztec civilization and its collapse following Spanish conquest, has been housed in France's Bibliothèque Nationale since 1898—but spent decades outside Mexico even before that. Now, thanks to a diplomatic agreement marking 200 years of Franco-Mexican relations, the invaluable document will be exhibited at Mexico City's National Museum of Anthropology, allowing Mexicans to see their own history in their own country.

The exchange reflects a broader shift in cultural diplomacy. French President Emmanuel Macron and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum arranged this temporary swap during Macron's visit to Mexico last year. In return for the Codex Azcatitlán, Mexico will lend France the Codex Boturini, another priceless document whose pictograms chronicle the Aztec migration to Lake Texcoco and the founding of Tenochtitlán. Both codices remain among the world's most important firsthand accounts of pre-Columbian Mesoamerica.

This moment also reflects Mexico's intensified efforts to reclaim its cultural heritage. The country has long campaigned for the return of artifacts removed during centuries of colonial history. Last year alone, Mexico's ministry of foreign relations successfully repatriated more than 2,000 objects. While the Codex Azcatitlán's display in Mexico is temporary, the agreement demonstrates that dialogue and mutual respect can help bridge the gap between nations and restore pieces of history to their communities of origin.
quick_facts: Codex Azcatitlán held in France's Bibliothèque Nationale since 1898
First display in Mexico in 186 years, opening at National Museum of Anthropology
16th-century pictographic account of Aztec fall to Spanish conquistadors
Exchange marks 200 years of Franco-Mexican diplomatic relations
Mexico repatriated over 2,000 cultural objects last year
